cards.front: circuit
cards.back: A path that electricity can travel around.
cards.say: circuit. A path that electricity can travel around. A torch has a circuit inside.

cards.front: complete circuit
cards.back: A circuit with no gaps, so electricity can flow all the way round.
cards.say: complete circuit. A circuit with no gaps, so electricity can flow all the way round. A bulb lights up in a complete circuit.

cards.front: cell
cards.back: A part that gives energy to a circuit. People often call it a battery.
cards.say: cell. A part that gives energy to a circuit. People often call it a battery. A torch needs a cell to work.

cards.front: battery
cards.back: Two or more cells joined together.
cards.say: battery. Two or more cells joined together. A remote control uses a battery.

cards.front: bulb
cards.back: A part that gives out light when electricity flows through it.
cards.say: bulb. A part that gives out light when electricity flows through it. The bulb in my torch is bright.

cards.front: wire
cards.back: A part that carries electricity around the circuit.
cards.say: wire. A part that carries electricity around the circuit. The wire joins the cell to the bulb.

cards.front: switch
cards.back: A part that opens or closes a circuit to turn it on or off.
cards.say: switch. A part that opens or closes a circuit to turn it on or off. I press the switch to turn on the light.

cards.front: buzzer
cards.back: A part that makes a sound when electricity flows through it.
cards.say: buzzer. A part that makes a sound when electricity flows through it. The buzzer in the alarm is loud.

cards.front: motor
cards.back: A part that spins when electricity flows through it.
cards.say: motor. A part that spins when electricity flows through it. A motor makes the toy fan spin.

cards.front: What does a bulb need to light up?
cards.back: A complete circuit with a cell and no gaps.
cards.say: What does a bulb need to light up? A complete circuit with a cell and no gaps.

cards.front: Why does a bulb not light if there is a gap in the circuit?
cards.back: The electricity cannot flow all the way round.
cards.say: Why does a bulb not light if there is a gap in the circuit? The electricity cannot flow all the way round.

cards.front: What does a closed switch do?
cards.back: It completes the circuit so electricity flows.
cards.say: What does a closed switch do? It completes the circuit so electricity flows.

cards.front: What does an open switch do?
cards.back: It makes a gap, so electricity cannot flow.
cards.say: What does an open switch do? It makes a gap, so electricity cannot flow.

cards.front: Is a circuit with an open switch on or off?
cards.back: Off.
cards.say: Is a circuit with an open switch on or off? Off.

cards.front: What happens to a bulb if you add a second bulb in the same loop?
cards.back: Both bulbs are dimmer.
cards.say: What happens to a bulb if you add a second bulb in the same loop? Both bulbs are dimmer.

cards.front: What happens if you add another cell to a circuit with one bulb?
cards.back: The bulb gets brighter.
cards.say: What happens if you add another cell to a circuit with one bulb? The bulb gets brighter.

cards.front: Which circuit part carries electricity?
cards.back: The wires.
cards.say: Which circuit part carries electricity? The wires.

cards.front: Which part is the energy supply?
cards.back: The cell or battery.
cards.say: Which part is the energy supply? The cell or battery.

cards.front: Name three things a circuit can power.
cards.back: A bulb, a buzzer and a motor.
cards.say: Name three things a circuit can power. A bulb, a buzzer and a motor.

cards.front: Why should you never touch mains electricity?
cards.back: It is very dangerous and can badly hurt or kill you.
cards.say: Why should you never touch mains electricity? It is very dangerous and can badly hurt or kill you.

cards.front: Which is safe to use in a school circuit, a cell or a wall socket?
cards.back: A cell. A wall socket is dangerous.
cards.say: Which is safe to use in a school circuit, a cell or a wall socket? A cell. A wall socket is dangerous.

cards.front: Why is a switch useful?
cards.back: It lets us turn something on and off easily.
cards.say: Why is a switch useful? It lets us turn something on and off easily.

cards.front: What do we call a drawing of a circuit with symbols?
cards.back: A circuit diagram.
cards.say: What do we call a drawing of a circuit with symbols? A circuit diagram.

cards.front: True or false: A circuit works when it has a gap.
cards.back: False. A gap stops electricity from flowing.
cards.say: True or false: A circuit works when it has a gap. False. A gap stops electricity from flowing.
